alex: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on SM92 after the kernel selector changes for quantized picks. Sequence-dependent path is flipping between fp8 and int4 kernels and we're seeing latency spikes around seqlen ~512-768 when batch sizes > 8. Profiling below.

alex: ```perf
env: sm92, cuda 12.2
model: redwood-omni-3b-quant
seq: 768 -> avg tail latency +18% vs baseline
kv: cold->warm transition shows extra memcpy + kernel recompile
kernel picks: fast_fp8_attn (short), slow_int4_attn (long)
batch: 12
```

maria: :eyes: can you paste the kernel selection trace and nvprof summary (or cupy profiler output)? is the selector switching mid-request or only between requests?

alex: Trace shows a switch inside the same stream when the runtime reallocs workspace on the first large token after kv-warmup. Not mid-token, but mid-generation which causes a synchronous memcpy and stalls the stream.

jon: I instrumented kernel_selector yesterday — looks like the hysteresis threshold is too tight. It picks based on seq_boundary ~640 and immediately flips to the int4 path; that path disables kv_prefetch (to save memory) which causes the memcpy. We need a per-arch margin so sm92 doesn't flip at those seqs.

samira: Proposal: autotune per-arch hysteresis and add a holdback window to avoid switching mid-request. Suggested params: hysteresis_ms=30, seq_margin=128, min_batch_for_fp8=4, kv_warmup_steps=2. Also add a step count fallback so we don't recompile/switch until kv cache stabilized.

alex: Also saw intermittent OOMs on int4 path at batch 16 on 80GB cards — the workspace heuristic for int4 is too optimistic when combined with tensor-core workspace for fp8 kernels that get chosen in mixed batches. Attached snippet: 

alex: ```text
[OOM] sm92 device0: requested workspace 24.3GB available 23.8GB (batch=16, seq=1024, model=redwood-omni-3b-quant-int4)
stack: runtime::alloc_workspace -> kernel_launch -> kernel_selector::pick
```

jon: I'll run a systematic sweep: seqlens [64,128,256,512,768,1024] x batches [1,2,4,8,12,16], record kernel choices, workspace usage, and p50/p95/p99 latencies. I'll enable a flag to holdback mid-request switching: `--holdback-midrequest=true`.

maria: Add a perf-regression detector in the sweep harness: if tail latency diverges >10% from baseline for any (seq,batch) mark config unsafe. Also collect kernel compile times and number of reallocs per request.

perf-bot: scheduled job #sm92-quant-sweep-1815 in 10m. Will post CSV to /artifacts/perf/sm92/1815000000.csv when done. :robot_face:

samira: For autotuner, we should expose per-arch knobs: seq_margin (samples), hysteresis_ms (ms), min_batch_for_quant_path, kv_warmup_steps, workspace_headroom_pct. Default table per-arch: sm83->{seq_margin:64,hysteresis_ms:20}, sm86->{96,25}, sm92->{128,30}. We'll let autotune refine these by workload.

alex: One more safety idea — add a "graceful fallback" mode where if a switch causes >5% latency regression within next N tokens we auto-revert to previous kernel and mark pairing as suspect for that model+arch+seq. Avoids noisy rollouts.

maria: :thumbsup: sounds good. jon — can you include that revert check in the sweep script so we log failures?

jon: yup. will run with revert-check and upload logs. planning to run the canary on a dedicated cluster first.

alex: I'll open the PR for selector changes and include unit tests + integration perf test. tagging @eng-sre for canary scheduling.

samira: Thanks — once we have CSV we can feed it to optimize engine to propose per-arch defaults and an initial holdback policy.

alex: Cool. keeping this thread for traceability. :thumbsup:
